mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week trend of increasing RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -16.3% to -12.0%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue over the next four weeks, driving further gains.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from -20.6% to -13.7% in the last week suggests a critical mass of people returning to offices, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation visits during weekdays.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a week-on-week WORKPLACES increase of more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with an increase in TRANSIT station visits signifies a broader shift away from home-bound activities and towards out-of-home engagement, directly boosting retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling and TRANSIT mobility rising compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, the consistent and recent acceleration of GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates a baseline level of public comfort and activity that will extend to non-essential retail and recreation as confidence grows over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above its pre-period baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp increase in TRANSIT station visits in the most recent week, from -50.7% to -45.6%, suggests a rapid return to public transport use which will immediately facilitate increased access to retail and recreation venues in the short term.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 4 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a week-on-week TRANSIT increase of more than 4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating less time spent at home, directly correlates with more time spent in public spaces, which will translate to higher retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The combined strong rebound in WORKPLACES mobility and the sustained positive trend in GROCERY_PHARM indicate a return to both work and essential errands, creating more opportunities and reasons for people to also engage in retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES is above -15% AND GROCERY_PHARM is above 0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks when WORKPLACES is above -15% and GROCERY_PHARM is above 0%.

mechanism_narrative: While PARKS mobility is still negative, its recent improvement from -30.7% to -27.7% suggests increasing comfort with outdoor public spaces, likely due to seasonal changes, which often precedes or accompanies a broader willingness to visit other public retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows a positive week-on-week change for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite PARKS mobility showing two consecutive weeks of positive change.
